hints: The three coplanar forces are in equilibrium, so both the net horizontal component and the net vertical component must equal zero: $\Sigma F_x = 0$ and $\Sigma F_y = 0$.
Resolve horizontally: force $P$ is vertical and has no horizontal component, so the horizontal components of the $3\text{ N}$ and $2\text{ N}$ forces balance: $2\cos\theta = 3\cos 60^\circ$.
Resolve vertically: the downward force $P$ balances the sum of the upward vertical components of the other two forces: $P = 3\sin 60^\circ + 2\sin\theta$.
walkthrough:
Resolve forces horizontally in equilibrium, noting that the vertical force $P$ has zero horizontal component:
$$\Sigma F_x = 0 \implies 2\cos\theta = 3\cos 60^\circ$$
$$2\cos\theta = 3(0.5) = 1.5$$

Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium:
$$\Sigma F_y = 0 \implies P = 3\sin 60^\circ + 2\sin\theta$$
$$P = 3\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) + 2\sin 41.4096^\circ$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the conditions for static equilibrium of coplanar forces:
$$\Sigma F_x = 0 \quad \text{and} \quad \Sigma F_y = 0$$
By resolving along the horizontal axis, the unknown vertical force $P$ does not enter the equation.

Equate the opposing horizontal components:
$$2\cos\theta = 3\cos 60^\circ$$
Substitute the exact value $\cos 60^\circ = 0.5$:
$$2\cos\theta = 3 \times 0.5 = 1.5$$
Divide both sides by $2$:
$$\cos\theta = \frac{1.5}{2} = 0.75$$
Take the inverse cosine:
$$\theta = \cos^{-1}(0.75) \approx 41.4096^\circ \approx 41.4^\circ$$

Resolve forces vertically, setting the downward force $P$ equal to the sum of the upward vertical components:
$$P = 3\sin 60^\circ + 2\sin\theta$$
Substitute $\theta = 41.4096^\circ$:
$$\sin 60^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \approx 0.866025$$
$$\sin 41.4096^\circ = \sqrt{1 - \cos^2\theta} = \sqrt{1 - 0.75^2} = \sqrt{0.4375} \approx 0.661438$$

ai_rubric.Applying Coplanar Equilibrium: Resolves horizontally to get $2\cos\theta = 3\cos 60^\circ \implies \theta = 41.4^\circ$, and vertically to get $P = 3\sin 60^\circ + 2\sin\theta = 3.92\text{ N}$.
ai_rubric.Resolving Forces Along Chosen Axes: Decomposes the coplanar forces into horizontal and vertical components to find both unknowns.
